text:
alex: Acme says their traffic started getting 401s immediately after rotating their API key. They see the new key in the dashboard as active but curl from their CI still returns invalid_api_key.
alex: Repro steps they gave: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <NEW_KEY>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat --header 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
alex: Response snippet from their logs: 
```
HTTP/2 401
content-type: application/json
x-edge-instance: eu-rt-03
{"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key not found"}
```
maria: Do they have any proxies or long-lived connections between clients and our edge? That header x-edge-instance makes me think they hit the same edge backend repeatedly.
alex: Yes — they said it's an internal service that keeps HTTP/2 keepalives to reduce latency. They rotate key in place but don't restart the service.
maria: Ah — sounds like an auth header cached on the upstream connection. Some HTTP/2 connection pools reuse the original headers (or the service keeps an Authorization header attached to the connection) so when the token rotates the connection still supplies the old header to the edge. That would cause 401 even though the dashboard shows the new key active.
alex: Quick check — asked them to run with Connection: close and retry. They sent this: 
```
curl -v --http2-prior-knowledge -H 'Authorization: Bearer <NEW_KEY>' -H 'Connection: close' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
support-bot: Reaction :thumbsup: from customer.
acme-note (reported by alex): After sending with Connection: close the request succeeds.
maria: Good repro. Workaround is to restart their client process (or close pooled connections) after key rotation, or send with Connection: close for a rolling update.
maria: For a long-term fix we should consider making rotation invalidate cached per-connection auth at the edge. Can runtime-oncall weigh in on whether our edge reuses connection-level cached headers?
runtime-oncall: Confirmed — our edge can attach downstream's Authorization to an upstream connection pooling layer in some proxy configs. There isn't currently a forced revalidation when a key is rotated.
runtime-oncall: Immediate mitigation we can do: when a key is rotated via dashboard we can emit a small event to trigger closing pooled backend connections for that org on the edge. Filing ENG-1429 to track.
alex: Filed ENG-1429 and shared repro (curl + logs). Adding them to the ticket.
maria: Also document a short KB for customers: "After rotating API keys, restart services that maintain persistent connections or reuse connection pools; alternatively perform a short rolling restart or include Connection: close for the next request."
alex: I've sent the KB draft to support docs and included the workaround. Customer confirmed temp fix and will do rolling restart.
runtime-oncall: Marking for postmortem follow-up — adding to oncall board.
alex: Closing thread from support side, will update ENG-1429 with progress and notify the customer when edge change is deployed. :white_check_mark:
